title: Sarah A Probable NDE 6351
content: It may be useful to note that there has been no history of heart problems in my family and I myself have always been reasonably healthy, enjoying a regular swim. Two days prior to the incident, I had been to my doctor for a feeling of ‘tight chested-ness’. I was given an electro-cardiogram, which identified sinus tachycardia and a right bundle branch block. The doctor wasn't too concerned but advised that if the condition worsened I should report to hospital; otherwise, I should see him in the morning for another electro-cardiogram and to discuss the matter further. The next day, I went back to my doctor who conducted another electro-cardiogram and made an appointment with the Chief consultant Cardiologist at the region’s hospital. Again, I was advised to report into hospital with anything unusual. I didn't bother. I went to bed the night before the cardiology appointment, in an extremely mournful state. It was as if I knew I was going to die, not because I was worried, but because it’s what I wanted. Earlier in the day I’d had a feeling of extreme sadness. I welcomed death with open arms because I felt my life to be truly useless, insubstantial and ineffectual. It may seem cliché to say so, but I was dying of a broken heart. It was the proverbial straw that broke the camel’s back. I had been struggling to gain the recognition that I supposed I deserved academically, socially or as a person in my own right. Some of my work had been stolen, someone broke into my home, I had my car vandalized, and I had been attacked on the street. It seemed as though everything was being thrown at me at once. I was utterly tired of this life. I was tired of a competitive, degenerate rat race of corrupt winners and idealistic losers. Pain, both physical and emotional overwhelmed me and I began to realize that I really was dying but that I wasn't afraid. As I surrendered in my bed, I began to shake and gasp for air; my chest was bursting as my ribs seemed to constrict around my body, I could feel my heart racing as though it was in my throat and I would have been shouting had my voice not been quelled for lack of air. I lost consciousness. I became aware of a strange noise which grew louder and louder. I thought I was ‘waking up’ only what I saw was certainly not what I had expected! I did ‘wake up’; only to realize that the strange noise I could hear was an incredible ‘unearthly’ singing. The music was so phenomenally beautiful that I could not reproduce it. I do not consider myself a culturally ignorant individual but this was nothing like any music I had ever heard. It was not as one might imagine as ‘heavenly’ or ‘choral’. Instead, it was beyond adequate description. Glorious beyond merit, the sound was celebratory and powerful. I couldn't make out was being said, not the language within it was projected. Upon my ‘waking’ to this music, I could see a great marble plaza with what appeared to be a militaristic formation but instead of marching, they were dancing and leaping ecstatically. All was bright and incredibly colorful as if the air were free of humidity and shadow, almost as if I were seeing in a form of ‘high definition’. Then I heard a voice of no discernible origin, neither masculine nor feminine but pleading. ‘Please don’t die, we need you; please don’t die’ it said. I asked, ‘what’s going on?’ The voice replied, ‘They are praising you’. I answered, astounded ‘Who, me?’ ‘Yes, you are needed.’ said the voice. I was taken aback as to why anyone should say such a thing. Normally I’d not be inclined to believe sycophantic nonsense such as compliments, but instead I felt it were the most genuine thing I’d ever been told. It was as if I had been told, ‘you are loved’ in a diplomatic sense (which is wise, given my reserved temperament). I heard the voice again as I listened to the music. ‘Please don’t die, we need you’. I agreed that I wouldn't choose to die and thanked them for being so kind to me. I had no idea anyone gave a sh#t. I realized that I was waking up for a second time and the music faded until I stood up from my bed, my face wet with tears. Who were they? A thought went through my mind: 'They're the ‘kachina’. But what or who are the kachina? I would later find out. [Editor’s note: Kachina are supernatural beings believed by the Hopi Indians to be ancestors of living humans.] I went to my hospital appointment for yet another electro-cardiogram and saw the consultant cardiologist. I didn't dare tell him what had happened. I had taken some notes with me on my condition and prepared to discuss treatment options. The meeting took about five minutes. The consultant looked at my electro-cardiogram and told me that there was nothing wrong with me. I felt embarrassed, very embarrassed. Had I wasted this individual’s time? ‘How is this possible?’ I asked. ‘All I know is that your test results and electro-cardiogram are normal and you won’t need any treatment’ he reported. I was told that the other electro-cardiogram’s were inexplicable and how I had been feeling, was simply a mystery. I left the hospital confused and feeling like some attention-seeking hypochondriac. I almost felt guilty that I wasn't ill! After all the trouble I’d caused everyone! There appeared to be no known reason why I should have experienced the heart attack and no known medical reason why or how I could have recovered fully from the heart condition. I can only surmise that I had a NDE: an experience that brought me back from the brink of that next, more desirable and glorious life. I learned that to renounce a life in material existence is easy in comparison to renouncing a life in blissful heaven. To give blood, to shed the mantle of gross matter, is far easier in comparison to receiving it. If I had to give the event a religious or spiritual context, I have been told that the experience is the ‘transverberation of the heart’. [Editor’s note: Transverberation is a wounding of the heart.] For me, it was a confirmation that I was still useful and that compassion was a force still extant.

diagnosis.diagnosis_raw: Sinus tachycardia and a right bundle branch block on ECG; later describes having experienced a 'heart attack' and a 'heart condition'.
diagnosis.disease_name: Sinus tachycardia with right bundle branch block; possible acute cardiac event (self-described as heart attack)
diagnosis.severity_description: Acute episode with loss of consciousness and severe chest symptoms; later stated full recovery
diagnosis.quality_of_life_impact: Lost consciousness; shaking, gasping for air, chest pain/pressure and racing heart sensation
diagnosis.disease_duration_before_healing: Two days prior to the incident she sought care for 'tight chested-ness'; the acute episode occurred the night before cardiology appointment.

treatment.treatments_raw: No treatment given; cardiologist said no treatment needed.

remission_outcome.time_to_remission_raw: By the cardiology appointment the next day, ECG/test results were normal.
remission_outcome.verification_detail: Multiple ECGs: initial ECGs showed sinus tachycardia and right bundle branch block; subsequent consultant cardiologist visit showed normal ECG/test results and no treatment needed.
remission_outcome.physician_quote: “All I know is that your test results and electro-cardiogram are normal and you won’t need any treatment”

agency_examples: Saw doctor twice for ECGs and attended cardiology consultant appointment
Prepared notes and planned to discuss treatment options
turner_factors.agency_details: Engaged medical evaluation and prepared to discuss treatment options, though she did not report to hospital during the acute episode.
intuition_examples: Felt as if she knew she was going to die the night before the appointment
turner_factors.intuition_details: Reported a foreboding sense she would die (and welcomed it) prior to losing consciousness.
turner_factors.emotional_release_details: Extreme sadness and surrender; awoke with face wet with tears.
positive_emotion_practices: Expressed thanks to the voice/beings; felt loved/needed; regained sense of usefulness/compassion
turner_factors.spiritual_practices_raw: Interpreted event as NDE; spiritual framing ('transverberation of the heart'); sense of being loved/needed; compassion as a force.
turner_factors.purpose_details: The voice said “Please don’t die, we need you”; she took this as confirmation she was still useful.

pre_illness_state.pre_illness_description: Reported prolonged struggle for recognition and multiple adverse events (work stolen, home break-in, car vandalized, attacked on the street) leading to extreme sadness and desire to die.
pre_illness_state.stress_description: Multiple stressors and assaults clustered together; felt overwhelmed by 'rat race' and corruption.
pre_illness_state.loss_description: Loss of safety and sense of meaning; work stolen; home invaded; attacked.
pre_illness_state.conflict_description: Struggle for recognition/validation and disillusionment with competitive social environment.
pre_illness_state.patient_causal_belief: Felt she was 'dying of a broken heart' and that her life felt useless/ineffectual amid overwhelming stress and pain.

existential_shift.identity_shift_description: Shift from feeling useless/ready to die to feeling loved/needed and oriented toward compassion.
existential_shift.surrender_description: In bed she surrendered, welcomed death, then lost consciousness.
existential_shift.transformation_narrative: She welcomed death due to despair, then after the experience felt loved/needed and concluded compassion still mattered; she chose not to die.
existential_shift.pivot_point_description: Hearing the voice: “Please don’t die, we need you; please don’t die” and being told “They are praising you.”
existential_shift.transformation_timing: The experience occurred during the loss-of-consciousness episode; by the next-day cardiology appointment her ECG was normal.

anomalous_experience.experience_description: During unconsciousness she perceived unearthly singing, a bright marble plaza with ecstatic dancing beings, and heard a pleading voice saying she was needed and being praised; she then returned to waking consciousness.
anomalous_experience.experience_timing: During the acute nighttime episode with loss of consciousness, the night before cardiology appointment.
anomalous_experience.message_content: “Please don’t die, we need you” and “Yes, you are needed.”

correspondential_markers.proprium_description: Strong concern with recognition/validation ('recognition that I supposed I deserved academically, socially or as a person in my own right').
correspondential_markers.self_attack_description: Self-worth collapse: described life as useless/ineffectual; later guilt/embarrassment for 'causing trouble' and feeling like a hypochondriac.
correspondential_markers.correspondence_notes: Narrative frames event as 'dying of a broken heart' (emotional/spiritual despair) coinciding with cardiac symptoms and subsequent shift to feeling loved/needed and valuing compassion.
correspondential_markers.resolution_type: Surrender/acceptance of death followed by renewed sense of purpose, love, and compassion.

validation.statistical_improbability_notes: ECG abnormalities (sinus tachycardia and RBBB) reported on prior tests, followed by normal ECG at consultant visit without treatment; however, the exact medical diagnosis ('heart attack') is self-described and lacks objective confirmation details beyond ECG statements.
validation.extraction_notes: Narrative uses 'heart attack' colloquially; objective details include ECG findings and later normal ECG per cardiologist. Remission verification method coded as blood_markers due to schema limits, but the explicit test is ECG.

analysis.case_summary: After ECGs showed sinus tachycardia and right bundle branch block and she experienced a nighttime episode with severe chest symptoms and loss of consciousness accompanied by an NDE, she attended a cardiology appointment the next day where the consultant reported her ECG/test results were normal and no treatment was needed.
key_healing_factors: Near-death experience with explicit message to live ('Please don’t die, we need you')
Surrender/acceptance of death followed by renewed will to live
unique_features: Cardiac symptoms/ECG abnormalities followed by rapid normalization without treatment, temporally linked to an NDE
Voice identified her as 'needed' and 'praised' amid celebratory music/visions
analysis.analysis_notes: This is primarily an NDE narrative with a possible rapid resolution of a cardiac abnormality; it is not a cancer/remission case. Medical documentation is limited to ECG descriptions and a cardiologist’s verbal conclusion.
